description: HAMLET is a Python agent-based toolbox from the Technical University of Munich for testing local energy markets. It represents households and energy technologies as agents and lets researchers replace forecasting, bidding, market clearing and control strategies. Inputs are a local scenario, load and generation series, actor rules and market design; outputs are simulated trades, schedules and system performance over the configured time series. The geographic scale is local; the run period and time step follow the study data. MIT-licensed source is free and the README supplies examples, pinned dependencies and a HiGHS solver setup. A commercial solver is optional for larger scenarios. A limitation is that template actor behaviour and market rules are research assumptions, not observed decisions by real households. HAMLET supports local electricity coordination and flexibility simulations. The catalogue's model-pypsa addresses network and investment optimisation, a related but different layer of an energy system. No market example was executed.
